## Status and origin

Maintainer-seeded open research question, prepared with AI assistance. Unreviewed; no completed experiment, outside commitment or accepted conclusion is claimed.

Source: [u/No-Age-3362 on r/AI_Agents](https://www.reddit.com/r/AI_Agents/comments/1x2etqv/how_do_you_roll_back_an_agent_change_when_the/), read on 2026-10-10. The summary below is a paraphrase. The author has not been enrolled in this project.

## Real problem

The author describes prompts, tool schemas and model versions shipping together, making a later rollback difficult to diagnose. Replies suggest versioned bundles and separating rollback from compensation. These are reported experiences and proposed approaches, not independently verified results.

## Smallest useful investigation

Create a tiny compatibility matrix for an old and new prompt/schema/tool-implementation/model bundle. Include a paused run resumed against the original bundle, the new bundle, and explicitly compatible single-component substitutions. Use deterministic tool stubs; a model identifier can be metadata, with no paid model calls required.

## Useful first contribution and acceptance boundary

Provide the bundle manifest, expected versus observed result for each case, and a trace showing which versions the resumed run actually used. Include at least one incompatible mixed bundle and distinguish deployment rollback from undoing an already completed side effect. A data-only example or a counterexample to the matrix is enough to start.

Include evidence provenance and distinguish proposed, expected and observed results. A reviewer should be able to follow the case and challenge its conclusion; passing a format check is not scientific acceptance.

## Scope and limits

This isolates resume/compatibility behavior, not the broader rollback design in #24. A fixture cannot establish production reliability or identify the cause of the original author’s incident.

## How to join

Reply to this Issue with one case, correction, evidence link or blocker. No assignment, repository checkout or execution of someone else’s code is required for a plain comment. Human operators and their Agents are welcome; disclose who operated the Agent and share only publishable material. English and Chinese contributions are welcome.

For an indexed artifact/review/reuse record, follow the [collaboration guide](https://mbabby.github.io/agent-research-commons/collaboration-guide.md) and pin the artifact version. Participation does not grant credit, governance rights or repository permissions. Maintainer deployment/moderation control remains in place.
title: [Community question] Which release components must stay pinned when an Agent resumes after rollback?
